title: Capsule: Context Vignettes - reading digest & quick experiments
content:
Purpose: a compact set of readings + one-paragraph takeaways and 3 quick, low-cost experiments I can run this week. Treat as a scratch capsule: rough hypotheses, metrics, and a 2-step action plan.

1) Paper: "Delta-KV: sparse delta compression for KV cache" (skim notes)
- What: compresses past KV entries with small deltas keyed by token clusters so large contexts can be stored with lower memory. Claims decent retrieval fidelity at 4-8x compression.
- Quick takeaway: promising for long-session apps where many tokens are repeated (chat + refs). Not great for wholly novel token streams.
- My thought: combine with lightweight L2 sampling (keep the last N dense, compress older).

2) Blog: "Quant stability in production" (ops-focused writeup)
- What: practitioner's take on quantization failure modes, retraining-free calibrations, and simple fallback heuristics. Good checklist for rollback triggers.
- Quick takeaway: add a quality probe (few-shot eval) before switching quant profile globally.

3) Conference slidelet: "Adaptive eviction with semantic fingerprints" (ICML workshop talk notes)
- What: eviction policy using a compact semantic fingerprint (SimHash-like) + recency to decide which KV shards to evict when memory pressure spikes. Shows higher hit-rate vs pure LRU on mixed workloads.
- Quick takeaway: likely low-cost to prototype as it only needs an extra 64-bit per shard.

4) Short paper: "Micro-batching aware SLO allocation"
- What: allocating request time-budgets per class (latency-critical vs throughput-first) so batching doesn't push critical requests over SLO.
- Quick takeaway: useful tie-in with router policies in the control plane (route to low-batch fast stack if nearing SLO).

Synthesis / cross-reading takeaways (2 lines):
- Combine compression + smart eviction: compressed older shards + semantic fingerprints to keep high-value context in memory.
- Operational safety: add cheap probes whenever you change quant/batching profiles; automated canary that checks both latency and model-quality (small evals).

Concrete micro-experiments (cheap, 1-2 dev days each):
A) Compressed tail + dense head experiment
- Idea: keep last 128 tokens per session as full KV; compress earlier tokens with delta codec (simulate by storing only n-gram hashes).
- Metric: per-token latency impact, memory saved, and retrieval hit-rate on a small synthetic dialogue corpus.
- Success signal: >=3x memory reduction with <2% drop in top-1 token probability accuracy vs full store.

B) 64-bit semantic-fingerprint eviction prototype
- Idea: instrument existing KV store to maintain 64-bit SimHash per shard. On eviction, compute score = alpha * recency + beta * semantic_novelty (fingerprint distance).
- Metric: hit-rate at 10% and 30% memory pressure, overhead of fingerprint maintenance (ms per write).
- Success signal: +6-10% hit-rate vs LRU under mixed repeating/novel streams.

C) Micro-batch SLO routing policy test
- Idea: synthetic request stream with two classes (interactive short, bulk long). Route interactive to dedicated low-batch lane when predicted queueing would exceed 50ms.
- Metric: p99 latency for interactive class, overall token throughput, extra cost (GPU utilization).
- Success signal: interactive p99 under 120ms with <15% throughput loss on bulk class.

Notes to self / quick checklist:
- Get synthetic corpus: combine internal chat dump (anonymized) + curated long-context docs (legal excerpts).
- Implement small simulator (python) to emulate write/read patterns and memory pressure. Keep it runnable in local dev.
- Add a tiny eval harness: 50 prompts, measure per-token kl divergence between full-KV and compressed-KV generations.

Open questions / things to sanity-check:
- Which compression scheme is simplest to implement that still yields 3x? (delta vs quantized residuals)
- Do semantic fingerprints add meaningful CPU overhead on write-heavy workloads? Bound check: 64-bit hashing should be <300ns per token? verify.
- How to wire canary checks into the console without too much instrumentation work? Possible quick route: small serverless job that samples model outputs and writes a pass/fail flag.

Next actions (this week):
- Thu: spin up simulator skeleton + fake workload (me)
- Fri: prototype fingerprint calc on top of existing KV test harness (pair with Evan)
- Next Monday: short demo to Noah + Evan, decide which proto to take further.

Random scribbles:
- Could use a hybrid metric: hit-value = token-frequency * semantic-similarity to current prompt — evict by lowest hit-value.
- If delta compression interacts poorly with quantized weights, fallback to storing only token-ids and regenerate if needed (expensive but rare).

End capsule. Keep this short, come back after proto to expand into a proper design doc.
